newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia condemns coverage of alleged CIA spy case.
newsitem.headline: Russia condemns coverage of alleged CIA spy case.

text.p: The Russian Foreign Ministry condemned on Thursday what it said were artificial attempts to sour relations with Washington over the case of a CIA station chief alleged to have spied for Moscow.

Ministry spokesman Mikhail Demurin said the United States had contacted Moscow in connection with the arrest of CIA employee Harold Nicholson on charges he had sold information to Russian agents, Russian news agencies said.
"We have no information confirming this version," they quoted Demurin as telling a briefing in Moscow.

He said the media were linking Nicholson's arrest to the failure of the so-called "Galkin case" -- a reference to former Soviet spy Vladimir Galkin, who was briefly held by the FBI in New York this month.

The U.S. dropped charges against Galkin of trying to obtain U.S. secrets, after Moscow protested Washington had broken an unwritten understanding protecting former agents from arrest and threatened to retaliate.
"For our part we are firmly against any attempts to artificially complicate Russian-American relations under any pretext," Demurin added, according to Interfax.
